The hard boundary is template system, hosting, domains, and very low maintenance, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Umso in an empty repository.
This system will serve as a fast, template-based website builder focused on simplicity and responsiveness, ideal for startups, SaaS landing pages, and professional portfolios.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: answer a few questions about your product/use-case, generate a clean responsive startup landing page from curated templates, edit copy/media inline, configure built-in features, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.

Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default (in SQLite) and make exporting a site configuration to a portable JSON file straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.

You must implement the following core capabilities, reflecting Umso's feature set:
1. Guided Generation: Provide a short initial wizard that asks for the project name and use case, then generates a tailored starting point.
2. Built-in Forms: Include a functional lead-collection form block that saves submissions to the local database.
3. Built-in Analytics: Create a simple, privacy-friendly analytics dashboard displaying page views and form submissions, without requiring third-party scripts.
4. Blog Integration: Add a lightweight Markdown-based blog engine to manage and render blog posts for SEO.
5. Section Library: Provide pre-designed, automatically responsive sections for hero, social proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
6. Design Constraints: Use a constrained design-token system for colors and typography rather than arbitrary CSS controls to ensure a professional look.
7. Multilingual Support: Include basic i18n scaffolding so pages can be translated and served in multiple languages.
8. Compliance & Privacy: Add an easily configurable built-in cookie banner for GDPR compliance.
9. Custom Code Injection: Allow users to paste custom <head> or <body> scripts/styles for advanced needs.

Editor Features:
- Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
- Provide a preview mode to toggle between desktop, tablet, and mobile widths, surfacing any overflow errors.

Technical Requirements:
- Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to platforms like Vercel or GitHub Pages.
- Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
- Add robust input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of missing data.
- Write focused tests for the core generation logic and one end-to-end happy path.
- Create a detailed README with setup, architecture, data location, and backup steps.

Explicit Exclusions:
- Do not add accounts, billing, centralized telemetry, or a hosted control plane.
- Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace, multi-tenant managed hosting, and advanced ecommerce features.

Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
